A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same structural-pruning work despite the revised title and organization. All 17 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including their figures, tables, equations and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning experiments, perplexity and zero-shot results, ablations, resource measurements and ten-run statistics in its main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds model evaluations, inference measurements, post-pruning fine-tuning experiments and moving-average-baseline ablations.

M1.justification: The Bernoulli-mask objective, policy-gradient updates, moving-average baseline, projection, initialization options and deterministic mask selection remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 clarifies existing hidden-state pruning; Appendix A.6 introduces an additional post-pruning fine-tuning evaluation.

E1.justification: v2 adds Alpaca instruction data for post-pruning fine-tuning in Appendix A.6. C4, WikiText2, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande and both ARC tasks were already used in v1, including Appendix G. The additional LLaMA-3 and Mistral checkpoints expand model settings.

E2.justification: Bonsai joins the main channel/head and initialization comparisons. The retained LLaMA-2 zero-shot comparison in Table A5 gains both Bonsai and Wanda-sp. Dense reference rows disappear from Tables 1–2, while the existing pruning comparators remain in corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds post-pruning LoRA fine-tuning and a separate inference evaluation using 2048-token sequences, batch size 4 and an A100 40GB GPU. It also evaluates LLaMA-3-8B and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, specifying a 6e-3 learning rate for LLaMA-3. The retained main experiments still use 128-token sequences and the original C4 calibration protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix A.10 newly tests removing the moving-average baseline and varying its window size and mask-sampling count. Table A8 reports, for example, perplexity of 185.87 without versus 52.23 with the baseline for LLaMA-2-13B at 50% pruning. Appendix A.6 additionally examines recovery after fine-tuning. Existing initialization, projection and global-versus-local analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same ten-run experiment with fixed initialization and identical means and standard deviations in Table A7. No additional uncertainty-reporting practice or significance testing is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for Bonsai, LLaMA-3, Mistral, fine-tuning, inference costs and baseline ablations. Common main-table scores remain unchanged, but Table A5 changes the proposed method's 50%-pruned LLaMA-2-7B WinoGrande accuracy from 52.40 to 52.64 and average from 41.14 to 41.19. Dense scores and v1's full 35%/45% comparison tables are removed; some intermediate-rate results remain in ablations.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a control-variate derivation covering unbiasedness, the optimal coefficient and variance reduction, then applies it to score-function gradients under an independent-baseline assumption. This formal analysis was absent from v1. The original projection theorem and policy-gradient derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the empirical superiority claim from perplexity to the majority of zero-shot tasks and include LLaMA-3 and Mistral. The central contributions of forward-only optimization, global heterogeneous pruning and flexible structural granularities remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of inference costs, architecture-dependent differences from SliceGPT, recovery after fine-tuning and sensitivity to baseline hyperparameters. It removes Remark 4's assertion that computation can be fully sparsified. The existing optimization-time, policy-gradient and domain-transfer limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly explains preserving block output dimensions and residual connections. It documents LoRA rank 16, alpha 10, 4,000 Alpaca samples, 1024-token sequences and PEFT defaults, plus hardware and batching for inference measurements. Core pruning settings remain documented, and both versions still promise future code release.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly contrasts Bonsai's utility-regression assumptions with the proposed optimization; v1 only cited Dery et al. generally. It adds references on mask learning, Gumbel-Softmax, policy-gradient baselines and the added models and data, while removing the Optimal Brain Surgeon reference. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The title and portions of the introduction and Gumbel-Softmax discussion are rewritten. Zero-shot evaluation gains a main-text subsection, and appendices A–J are substantially reordered into A.1–A.13 with a topical roadmap. The broader-impacts section is removed.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and headers, expands main tables, and adds perplexity columns to zero-shot displays. New tables cover inference, fine-tuning and ablations, and a new figure illustrates hidden-state pruning. v1's intermediate-rate comparison tables are removed; retained figures are relocated or revised in legends, axes and styling.

improvement.justification: The Bonsai comparisons, direct tests of the moving-average component, measured inference costs and fine-tuning recovery experiments substantially strengthen support for the paper's accuracy and practical-use claims. Removing dense references and intermediate-rate comparisons reduces context. The new theoretical argument also leaves its baseline-independence assumption unreconciled with Algorithm 1's current-sample baseline update. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial empirical strengthening.
